catalogue: Australian architectural paint, clear finishes, stains and installed wallcoverings

objects.name: architectural surface finish system
objects.definition: The coordinated preparation, primer or sealer, intermediate coats, finish coats or installed wallcovering that creates a completed decorative surface on a building substrate.
functions: Finish and protect a selected building surface
Keep substrate preparation and individual coating or covering layers explicit
Separate decorative appearance from weatherproofing, fire, wet-area and hazardous-material evidence

ncc_references.relationship: Ordinary decorative painting is treated differently from painting relied on to weatherproof an external wall; the latter remains compliance-sensitive construction requiring appropriate evidence.

cad.pattern: Bounded finish fields mapped to real substrate faces and interrupted at changes of system
cad.placement: On prepared walls, ceilings, trim, doors, timber, masonry and other selected hosts
cad.start: Prepared substrate or sound retained coating
cad.end: Exposed dry finish or installed wallcovering face
cad.opening: Cut around openings, fittings and excluded finishes
cad.load: Thin non-structural surface layers bonded to the host

notes: The selected substrate and exposure determine the coating system; appearance alone cannot choose compatible preparation or prove performance.

objects.name: internal wall paint system
objects.definition: A prepared internal wall surface carrying the selected primer, sealer or undercoat and one or more opaque decorative finish coats.
functions: Create a uniform internal wall finish
Protect the lining from ordinary service conditions
Coordinate local repairs, priming and complete finish-coat coverage

cad.pattern: Continuous wall fields divided at corners, openings and changes of colour or coating system
cad.placement: On prepared internal wall lining or solid substrate
cad.start: Floor, skirting or lower finish boundary
cad.opening: Exclude doors, windows, fittings and feature finishes as scheduled

notes: Low sheen, matt and other sheen descriptions are product attributes rather than separate wall solids.

objects.name: internal ceiling paint system
objects.definition: A prepared ceiling lining or solid soffit carrying compatible sealer or primer and opaque finish coats selected for overhead use.
functions: Create a uniform overhead finish
Limit visible joint and substrate variation only within the selected preparation and coating capability
Coordinate light fittings, vents, cornices and access panels
materials: flat or matt water-borne ceiling paint

cad.pattern: Continuous overhead fields divided at bulkheads, control joints and finish changes
cad.placement: On prepared plasterboard, fibre cement, concrete or other selected ceiling substrate
cad.opening: Cut around lights, grilles, access panels and penetrations

notes: Paint cannot correct framing, lining or joint geometry that remains outside the selected finish tolerance.

objects.name: internal trim paint system
objects.definition: A higher-contact opaque coating system applied to prepared skirtings, architraves, jambs, window boards, mouldings and similar internal trim.
functions: Protect handled and impact-prone trim surfaces
Provide a cleanable opaque finish
Coordinate joints, nail holes, caulk lines and adjoining wall finishes

cad.pattern: Coating follows each profiled trim face and return
cad.placement: On prepared skirting, architrave, jamb and moulding objects
cad.opening: Exclude hardware, gaskets and surfaces scheduled unpainted
cad.load: Thin finish following profiled host geometry

notes: The trim remains a board or moulding; its paint layers do not replace its physical profile.

objects.name: internal door paint system
objects.definition: The preparation, priming, undercoating and opaque finish coats applied to selected faces and edges of an internal door leaf and compatible frame or trim.
functions: Finish and protect the door surfaces
Maintain documented edge coverage
Coordinate hardware cut-outs, glazing, seals and unpainted moving interfaces

cad.pattern: Coating fields on leaf faces, edges, frame and selected trim
cad.placement: On the actual internal door leaf and frame surfaces
cad.opening: Exclude glazing, hardware, seals, labels and moving contact faces as documented
cad.load: Thin bonded finish moving with the leaf

notes: Painting an ordinary leaf does not create fire, smoke, acoustic or security performance.

objects.name: exterior wall paint system
objects.definition: A substrate-specific exterior preparation, primer and opaque finish-coat system applied to a wall cladding, render, concrete or masonry surface.
functions: Provide exterior colour and surface protection
Resist the selected weather exposure within documented product capability
Coordinate joints, flashings, penetrations and areas where coating contributes to weatherproofing
materials: elastomeric or texture coating where selected

ncc_references.relationship: Where paint is relied on for external-wall weatherproofing, evidence and the complete wall system matter; ordinary decorative painting is not enough.

cad.pattern: Continuous exterior coating fields following cladding, render or masonry geometry
cad.placement: On a compatible prepared external wall surface
cad.start: Wall base, flashing or coating boundary
cad.opening: Return and terminate around windows, doors, vents, joints and penetrations
cad.load: Thin bonded exterior coating exposed to weather

notes: A generic exterior acrylic layer cannot prove a wall's weatherproofing; substrate, joints, flashings and selected system remain visible.

objects.name: exterior timber opaque paint system
objects.definition: An opaque primer, undercoat and finish-coat build-up selected for exposed exterior timber boards, trim, doors or joinery.
functions: Shield timber from weather within documented capability
Provide opaque colour
Maintain coating continuity at faces, edges, ends and joints

cad.pattern: Coating follows every exposed board, moulding and end-grain face
cad.placement: On prepared exterior timber objects
cad.opening: Coordinate joints, cut ends, flashings and fixings

notes: Opaque paint hides grain but does not replace preservative treatment or repair decayed timber.

objects.name: smooth concrete or masonry coating system
objects.definition: A prepared concrete, render or masonry surface carrying pore treatment or sealer as needed and a smooth opaque coating build-up.
functions: Provide a smooth coloured finish
Control substrate suction through compatible preparation
Protect the surface within the selected coating's exposure class

cad.pattern: Continuous smooth coating field following concrete or masonry face
cad.placement: On prepared concrete, render or masonry
cad.opening: Interrupt at movement joints and excluded surfaces

notes: Paint should not bridge active cracks or hide unresolved water entry and efflorescence.

objects.name: concrete or masonry texture-coating system
objects.definition: A prepared concrete, render or masonry surface carrying compatible sealer, aggregate-filled texture layer and any documented protective topcoat.
functions: Create a selected relief texture
Reduce the visual prominence of minor substrate irregularity
Provide a durable coating build-up for the documented exposure

cad.pattern: Continuous raised-profile coating field with selected texture mapping
cad.placement: On prepared concrete, render or masonry
cad.opening: Stop at joints, flashings and finish boundaries

notes: Texture can mask minor appearance variation but cannot make loose render, active cracks or leaking construction sound.

objects.name: clear timber finish system
objects.definition: A prepared timber surface carrying a transparent or near-transparent sealer and protective film that leaves grain visible.
functions: Protect the timber surface
Retain visible timber grain and figure
Provide the selected sheen, colour shift and service resistance

cad.pattern: Transparent coating follows timber faces, profiles and edges
cad.placement: On prepared visible timber
cad.start: Prepared timber or compatible retained coating
cad.opening: Exclude hardware, seals and glue faces

notes: Clear does not mean colourless; timber, coating chemistry, ageing and film thickness can change appearance.

objects.name: penetrating timber oil finish system
objects.definition: A prepared timber surface treated with one or more penetrating oil coats that soak into surface fibres with little or no continuous surface film.
functions: Modify timber wetting and weathering behaviour within product capability
Enhance or retain visible grain
Provide a maintainable penetrating finish

cad.pattern: Thin absorbed treatment mapped to timber surface field
cad.placement: Within and immediately on prepared timber fibres
cad.opening: Exclude hardware and incompatible sealed areas
cad.load: Penetrating treatment rather than structural layer

notes: Oil, stain and varnish are not interchangeable names; store whether the selected product penetrates or forms a film.

objects.name: timber stain finish system
objects.definition: A prepared timber surface carrying a transparent or semi-transparent colour treatment, with any required compatible sealer or protective topcoat stored separately.
functions: Alter timber colour while retaining visible grain
Unify or deliberately vary appearance
Receive a compatible clear protective layer where the selected system requires it

cad.pattern: Colour treatment follows timber faces with grain visible
cad.placement: On prepared bare or compatible timber
cad.end: Stained face or clear protective film
cad.opening: Exclude glue faces and incompatible sealed zones
cad.load: Thin absorbed or low-build colour layer

notes: Final colour depends on timber species, age, preparation, absorption and coat count; a texture colour swatch is not a reliable material result.

objects.name: decorative effect paint system
objects.definition: A base coat, effect material and optional glaze or protective clear coat intentionally worked into a visible pattern, metallic, pearlescent, mottled or other decorative finish.
functions: Create a non-uniform decorative surface
Retain the physical base, effect and protective layers
Store application pattern separately from coating chemistry

cad.pattern: Layered procedural pattern over a bounded surface field
cad.placement: On prepared internal or selected external substrate
cad.end: Exposed effect or protective clear coat
cad.opening: Respect finish boundaries and sample-approved direction

notes: The SketchUp texture can represent appearance, but quantities and repair depend on the actual base, effect and topcoat layers.

objects.name: existing lead-paint encapsulation system
objects.definition: A documented existing-building management assembly in which a sound or stabilised lead-containing paint field is retained and enclosed beneath a compatible durable lead-free coating system.
functions: Retain a mapped hazardous existing coating without uncontrolled disturbance
Create a durable separating finish where the selected management plan permits
Keep lead evidence, retained layer and new encapsulating coats traceable

cad.pattern: Mapped retained hazardous coating field below a distinct new coating build-up
cad.placement: On surveyed existing building surfaces only
cad.start: Retained lead-paint field and stable boundary
cad.opening: Mark damaged, sampled, removed and inaccessible zones separately

notes: Lead content must come from competent assessment and evidence; age and colour alone are not enough.
This object records retained physical layers and the selected management route, not a DIY work instruction.

objects.name: installed wallcovering finish system
objects.definition: A prepared and sealed wall or ceiling surface carrying compatible adhesive and repeated wallpaper or specialty wallcovering drops with planned seams, pattern and trimmed edges.
functions: Provide a decorative sheet finish
Coordinate substrate preparation, adhesive and covering material
Preserve roll, drop, seam, pattern and edge geometry

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical or selected-direction drops with exact seams and pattern alignment
cad.placement: Over a smooth prepared and compatible wall or ceiling substrate
cad.opening: Trim around doors, windows, switches, outlets, vents and penetrations
cad.load: Light sheet finish bonded to the substrate

notes: Wallpaper is a finish over a lining or solid wall; it is not the lining itself.

objects.name: paste-the-wall wallcovering assembly
objects.definition: A wallcovering system in which adhesive is spread on the prepared wall immediately ahead of a dry non-woven or compatible covering drop.
functions: Bond dry drops using wall-applied adhesive
Permit pattern alignment and controlled sliding during placement
Keep adhesive field slightly ahead of each drop boundary

cad.pattern: Repeated dry drops over sequential wall-applied adhesive fields
cad.placement: On prepared wall or selected ceiling
cad.opening: Trim around fittings and openings

notes: Paste-the-wall describes adhesive placement, not the material appearance or pattern.

objects.name: paste-the-paper wallcovering assembly
objects.definition: A wallcovering system in which adhesive is applied to the back of each cut drop and the material is booked or rested where the selected product requires before hanging.
functions: Bond drops using backing-applied adhesive
Allow the selected covering to relax or expand before hanging
Coordinate paste coverage, booking and pattern alignment
materials: cellulose, starch, PVA or product-compatible adhesive

cad.pattern: Repeated pasted drops placed from a set-out line
cad.placement: On prepared and sized or primed wall
cad.opening: Trim around fittings and openings
cad.load: Adhesive bond distributed across drop backing

notes: Booking is an installation process state and is not a permanent extra folded layer in the completed model.

objects.name: ready-pasted wallpaper assembly
objects.definition: A wallpaper system using a factory-applied dry adhesive on the sheet backing that is activated in the manner specified for the selected product before hanging.
functions: Combine covering and factory adhesive coating
Activate the supplied adhesive
Create repeated pattern-matched drops without a separately spread site paste where documented

cad.pattern: Repeated drops carrying a factory adhesive backing
cad.placement: On prepared compatible wall after activation
cad.opening: Trim around fittings and openings
cad.load: Factory adhesive bonds covering to wall

notes: Pre-pasted normally requires activation; it is not the same adhesive topology as pressure-sensitive peel-and-stick film.

objects.name: self-adhesive wallcovering assembly
objects.definition: A wall film or covering supplied with a pressure-sensitive adhesive backing and temporary release liner, installed without wet paste.
functions: Combine decorative sheet and pressure-sensitive adhesive
Bond after release-liner removal
Allow repositioning or later removal only where the selected product states

cad.pattern: Repeated factory-adhesive panels
cad.placement: On smooth cured compatible painted or primed surface
cad.opening: Trim around fittings and openings

notes: The release liner is temporary packaging and is not part of the completed building model.
Removable is selected-product evidence, not a guarantee inferred from the adhesive name.

objects.name: specialty textile or natural-fibre wallcovering assembly
objects.definition: A prepared wall carrying product-specific adhesive and a textile, grasscloth, flock, metallic, linen-backed vinyl or other specialist wallcovering with sensitive face and seam requirements.
functions: Install a specialty decorative sheet material
Coordinate directional texture, panel shading and seams
Retain material-specific backing, adhesive and cleaning limits

cad.pattern: Repeated specialist drops with direction and shade metadata
cad.placement: On prepared wall with product-specific adhesive
cad.opening: Trim using product-specific detail around fittings and openings
cad.load: Light decorative sheet bonded to wall

notes: Natural fibres and handcrafted faces can show deliberate variation; the tool should not force a perfectly seamless repeated texture.

objects.name: multi-panel wall mural assembly
objects.definition: A wallcovering image divided across numbered or ordered panels whose seams and set-out reconstruct one continuous mural composition.
functions: Create one large composed image
Order and align multiple panels
Coordinate image crop, wall extent, openings and panel seams

cad.pattern: Ordered image panels rather than a repeating roll pattern
cad.placement: Within a nominated wall image boundary
cad.start: Image datum and first numbered panel
cad.opening: Crop or trim around openings as documented
cad.load: Light printed covering bonded to substrate

notes: A mural's visual continuity depends on panel order and crop; repeating pattern logic is not appropriate by default.

objects.name: retained existing paint film
objects.definition: An existing dry paint film deliberately left in place after its adhesion, condition and compatibility with the proposed system have been assessed.
functions: Remain as a bonded part of the recoating substrate
Carry compatible repair, primer or finish coats
Record boundaries between retained, feathered and removed coating

cad.pattern: Existing bounded film field with explicit retained and removed zones
cad.placement: On the original host beneath the new coating system
cad.opening: Respect repairs, penetrations and stripped areas

notes: Do not infer soundness, compatibility or lead content from colour, age or appearance alone.

objects.name: paint surface repair filler
objects.definition: A local filler used to restore small dents, holes, cracks or surface losses before priming and painting, without becoming the structural substrate.
functions: Restore local surface continuity
Provide a sandable paint-receiving patch
Keep repaired areas measurable and distinct from the surrounding substrate

cad.pattern: Local patches rather than a full-face layer
cad.placement: In prepared small defects below primer
cad.opening: Do not bridge movement joints

notes: A generic paint filler must not be used by the model to conceal unresolved movement, moisture damage or structural cracking.

objects.name: timber stopping putty
objects.definition: A small local stopping material pressed into nail holes, shallow checks and minor imperfections in timber or wood-based trim before an opaque or clear finish.
functions: Fill small timber-surface defects
Reduce visible fixing holes
Provide a finish-compatible local patch

cad.pattern: Small isolated plugs or patches
cad.placement: In prepared timber face below the selected finish
cad.opening: Exclude intended joints and drainage gaps

notes: Under a clear finish, colour and absorption may remain visible; opaque-paint stopping is not automatically suitable.

objects.name: paintable perimeter caulk
objects.definition: A flexible paint-compatible bead used at selected low-movement finish junctions such as trim-to-wall gaps before the final coating is applied.
functions: Close a selected visual gap
Maintain a flexible finish junction
Provide a paint-receiving bead where the product permits

cad.pattern: Continuous narrow bead
cad.placement: At nominated low-movement finish junction
cad.opening: Stop at intended gaps and movement joints

notes: The word caulk does not prove weather, fire, acoustic or waterproofing performance.

objects.name: masonry pore filler
objects.definition: A preparatory material worked into open pores, bugholes or a coarse mineral surface to reduce local voids before a smooth coating system.
functions: Reduce open surface voids
Create a more continuous paint-receiving face
Limit excessive local coating demand

cad.pattern: Full or local filled field following masonry face
cad.placement: Within open pores below sealer or finish
cad.opening: Do not fill designed joints or drainage paths

notes: Pore filling changes surface profile; it does not repair active cracks or prove water exclusion.

objects.name: local spot primer
objects.definition: Primer applied only to exposed repairs, bare patches, fixings or other local areas before the full coating schedule continues.
functions: Seal or prime isolated bare areas
Improve local adhesion
Reduce flashing or uneven absorption at repairs

cad.pattern: Isolated coating patches
cad.placement: Over local bare or repaired areas
cad.opening: Match actual exposed area

notes: Spot primer is a location-specific coat; it is not proof that the entire face received a primer coat.

objects.name: plasterboard sealer
objects.definition: A first coat selected to seal new plasterboard paper, stopped joints and local compounds so later coats meet a more consistent receiving surface.
functions: Reduce uneven suction
Bind the prepared surface
Provide a compatible base for internal finish coats

cad.pattern: Continuous first-coat field
cad.placement: Over the complete prepared plasterboard face
cad.opening: Exclude unpainted fittings and openings

notes: Sealer cannot turn a lower plasterboard finish level into a higher one or remove visible geometry under critical lighting.

objects.name: fibre-cement primer
objects.definition: A first coat selected for prepared fibre-cement sheet, board or trim before the compatible decorative coating build-up.
functions: Control substrate suction
Promote coating adhesion
Provide the specified base for internal or external finish coats

cad.pattern: Continuous face or selected edge coat
cad.placement: On prepared fibre-cement object
cad.opening: Follow sheet edges, joints and penetrations

notes: Model face, cut-edge and factory-applied treatments separately when the selected product system distinguishes them.

objects.name: alkali-resistant masonry primer
objects.definition: A primer selected to tolerate the alkaline character of prepared concrete, render or masonry and support the nominated coating system.
functions: Promote adhesion to mineral substrate
Reduce adverse alkaline interaction
Provide a consistent base for subsequent coats

cad.pattern: Continuous mineral-surface first coat
cad.placement: On sound dry prepared masonry, render or concrete
cad.opening: Stop at movement joints and excluded faces

notes: The label alkali-resistant does not permit coating uncured, wet or contaminated masonry without product evidence.

objects.name: timber primer
objects.definition: A first opaque coat selected to bond to prepared timber or wood-based substrate and receive the later undercoat and finish coats.
functions: Promote adhesion
Seal porous timber
Provide a compatible base for the opaque paint build-up

cad.pattern: Continuous first coat following timber faces and ends
cad.placement: On prepared timber below opaque coats
cad.opening: Treat cut ends, edges and joints as scheduled

notes: A factory primer remains its own known or unknown layer and must not be assumed compatible with every site-applied topcoat.

objects.name: architectural metal adhesion primer
objects.definition: A primer used on selected non-structural or ordinary architectural metal surfaces to establish adhesion for a decorative paint system.
functions: Promote adhesion to prepared metal
Isolate compatible substrate and finish chemistry
Support an ordinary architectural decorative coating build-up

cad.pattern: Continuous coat following prepared metal faces
cad.placement: On selected ordinary architectural metal
cad.opening: Exclude contacts and surfaces requiring another engineered system

notes: Long-term atmospheric corrosion protection for structural steel belongs to the AS/NZS 2312 protective-coating ontology, not this decorative primer object.

objects.name: galvanised-metal adhesion primer
objects.definition: A compatible primer applied to prepared galvanised or zinc-coated architectural metal where the selected decorative topcoat needs a separate adhesion layer.
functions: Bond the decorative system to the zinc-coated surface
Avoid incompatible coating contact
Provide a defined receiving coat for the topcoat

cad.pattern: Continuous primer on selected zinc-coated faces
cad.placement: On prepared galvanised architectural metal
cad.opening: Exclude unpainted contacts and drainage paths

notes: Do not erase the galvanised layer in the model; it remains the metal object's protective coating beneath this primer.

objects.name: timber knot sealer
objects.definition: A local barrier coat applied over resinous knots or similar timber features before an opaque coating system where the selected system requires it.
functions: Reduce local resin or stain migration
Isolate selected knots from later coats
Keep knot-treatment patches explicit

cad.pattern: Local patches over recorded knots
cad.placement: Between prepared timber and primer or undercoat as specified
cad.opening: Match actual knot geometry

notes: Knot sealer is a local treatment; it does not turn unsound or resin-wet timber into a suitable substrate.

objects.name: tannin-blocking primer
objects.definition: A barrier primer selected to limit tannin or other extractive staining from susceptible timber through an opaque coating system.
functions: Reduce extractive bleed
Provide a compatible opaque base
Record the area receiving barrier treatment

cad.pattern: Full-face or bounded barrier-primer field
cad.placement: On susceptible prepared timber below later opaque coats
cad.opening: Cover edges and ends as documented

notes: Tannin-blocking performance is product- and timber-dependent; do not infer it from a generic primer label.

objects.name: stain-blocking primer
objects.definition: A barrier primer applied to a prepared stained area to reduce migration of documented water, smoke, ink or other discolouration into later decorative coats.
functions: Isolate a documented discolouring contaminant
Provide a compatible receiving surface
Keep treated patches or fields identifiable

cad.pattern: Local patch or complete bounded barrier field
cad.placement: Over cleaned documented staining below the normal paint build-up
cad.opening: Extend only as investigation and product directions require

notes: The source of water, mould or contamination must be resolved; a stain blocker only manages later visual bleed.

objects.name: high-adhesion primer
objects.definition: A bonding primer selected for a sound but difficult-to-coat surface such as a dense, glossy or previously factory-finished substrate.
functions: Improve adhesion on a difficult substrate
Provide a compatible transition between unlike coating chemistries
Record where bonding treatment is required

cad.pattern: Continuous bonding field on nominated difficult substrate
cad.placement: Between prepared host and later coats
cad.opening: Exclude non-coatable seals and moving contacts

notes: High adhesion is a product claim requiring substrate-specific evidence, not a licence to omit cleaning or testing.

objects.name: combined primer-sealer-undercoat
objects.definition: One formulated coating documented to perform the selected priming, sealing and undercoating roles on a compatible substrate within a particular paint system.
functions: Prime the selected substrate
Reduce suction or bind the surface
Provide a uniform base for finish coats

cad.pattern: Continuous first or intermediate coat as scheduled
cad.placement: On the compatible prepared substrate
cad.opening: Follow paint-system boundaries

notes: The three words describe functions, not an instruction to draw three films when one physical application coat performs them.

objects.name: paint undercoat
objects.definition: An intermediate preparatory coat used beneath a finish coat to improve opacity, build, colour uniformity or compatibility within the selected paint system.
functions: Provide a uniform base colour
Build the coating system
Improve finish-coat appearance and coverage

cad.pattern: Continuous intermediate coating field
cad.placement: Between primer or sealed substrate and finish coat
cad.opening: Follow the system finish boundary

notes: Undercoat and primer can be separate products, one multi-role product or not both required; follow the documented system.

objects.name: paint intermediate coat
objects.definition: A coat positioned between the first preparatory coat and the exposed finish coat, used where the coating schedule requires extra build, opacity or performance.
functions: Increase system build
Improve opacity or continuity
Separate the first coat from the exposed finish

cad.pattern: Continuous coat field matching the selected paint system
cad.placement: Between preparatory and exposed coats
cad.opening: Follow system boundaries

notes: Intermediate describes sequence, not one universal paint chemistry.

objects.name: paint finish coat
objects.definition: The final exposed coat, or one of the exposed coats of the same finish product, that supplies the scheduled colour, sheen and service surface.
functions: Provide the visible colour and sheen
Form the exposed cleanable or weathering surface
Complete the documented coating schedule

cad.pattern: Exposed bounded coating field
cad.placement: Over compatible completed preceding coats
cad.opening: Return or terminate at openings as documented

notes: Two finish coats may be two application passes of one product; record coat count without inventing two different materials.

objects.name: opaque paint dry film
objects.definition: The permanent solid film left on a surface after an opaque architectural paint coat has dried or cured and its volatile carrier has departed.
functions: Remain as the physical coating layer
Carry colour, sheen and texture
Provide measurable dry-film build where the system requires it

cad.pattern: Very thin continuous planar film
cad.placement: On and conforming to the preceding substrate or coat
cad.opening: Exclude intentionally unpainted areas

notes: Wet-film thickness is an application measurement; the completed-building object is the dry film.

objects.name: timber grain filler
objects.definition: A material worked into open timber pores to produce a smoother face before a selected clear or opaque film finish.
functions: Fill open grain
Reduce visible pore relief
Support a smooth film-forming finish

cad.pattern: Thin pore-filled surface field
cad.placement: Within prepared open-grained timber beneath later finish
cad.opening: Follow the finished timber boundary

notes: Grain filler can alter colour and clarity; it is not automatically part of every clear timber system.

objects.name: timber sanding sealer
objects.definition: A seal coat formulated to raise or bind fibres and provide a readily sanded base before a compatible clear timber finish.
functions: Seal prepared timber
Provide a sandable intermediate surface
Support an even later clear coat

cad.pattern: Continuous clear or translucent preparation film
cad.placement: Between prepared timber and compatible clear topcoats
cad.opening: Follow finish boundaries

notes: Sanding sealer is system-specific and can weaken adhesion if inserted beneath an incompatible topcoat.

objects.name: retained lead-paint field
objects.definition: An existing coating field confirmed by suitable investigation to contain lead and deliberately retained as part of a documented management or encapsulation strategy.
functions: Record the hazardous existing coating extent
Remain beneath the management system
Prevent ordinary repaint logic from hiding a known lead-paint condition

cad.pattern: Survey-defined hazardous coating field
cad.placement: On the original substrate beneath retained management layers
cad.opening: Record interfaces, damage and removed zones

notes: Never infer lead from building age, paint colour or cracking alone; use documented investigation and competent hazardous-paint management.

objects.name: lead-paint encapsulating coating
objects.definition: A documented coating layer installed over suitable retained lead paint to form part of a surveyed encapsulation management system.
functions: Cover and isolate a suitable retained lead-paint field
Provide an inspectable management surface
Maintain the link to the underlying hazard record

cad.pattern: Continuous documented barrier field over confirmed retained hazard
cad.placement: Over only the surveyed and suitable retained lead-paint field
cad.opening: Detail edges, penetrations and damaged zones
cad.load: Thin management coating over hazardous existing film

notes: Encapsulation manages rather than removes the hazard; the underlying lead-paint object and inspection obligations remain in the model.

objects.name: wallcovering primer-sealer
objects.definition: A coating applied to a prepared wall to control porosity, improve adhesive behaviour and help later removal where supported by the wallcovering system.
functions: Create a uniform adhesive-receiving surface
Reduce excessive suction
Separate the wallcovering adhesive from the raw substrate

cad.pattern: Continuous primed wall field
cad.placement: On prepared wall beneath size or adhesive
cad.opening: Stop at fittings, openings and finish changes

notes: Primer, size and adhesive are different physical roles even when a proprietary product combines two of them.

objects.name: wallpaper size coat
objects.definition: A thin preparatory coat used in a selected wallpaper system to regulate suction, slip and adhesive working behaviour before hanging.
functions: Control adhesive absorption
Assist positioning and slip
Provide a system-specific preparation layer

cad.pattern: Thin complete preparation field
cad.placement: Between prepared wall or primer and wallcovering adhesive
cad.opening: Follow the wallcovering extent
cad.load: Thin preparatory dry or tacky coat

notes: Size is a trade term for this preparatory coating, not the width or height of the wallpaper.

objects.name: wallcovering adhesive film
objects.definition: The permanent cured or dried adhesive layer bonding an installed wallpaper or specialist wallcovering to its prepared substrate.
functions: Bond the covering to the wall
Transfer light service actions to the substrate
Preserve the selected paste-the-wall, paste-the-paper or factory-applied topology

cad.pattern: Continuous thin film behind each drop or panel
cad.placement: Between prepared wall and covering backing
cad.opening: Follow trimming and seam geometry

notes: Model the installed adhesive film, not temporary buckets, rollers, booking folds or release liners.

objects.name: water-borne acrylic wall paint
objects.definition: An opaque water-borne architectural coating with an acrylic or related polymer binder, commonly used as the exposed finish on prepared internal walls.
functions: Provide opaque colour
Create the scheduled sheen and cleanable face
Protect the prepared wall in ordinary internal service

cad.pattern: Continuous opaque internal wall field
cad.placement: Over the compatible sealed or primed wall
cad.opening: Cut around openings, trim and fittings

notes: Water-borne describes the application vehicle; the completed object is the dry polymer-pigment film.

objects.name: flat ceiling paint
objects.definition: An opaque architectural paint formulated and selected for ceilings, usually with a flat or matt appearance that limits reflected surface variation.
functions: Provide a uniform ceiling colour
Create a low-reflectance exposed face
Complete the ceiling coating system

cad.pattern: Continuous overhead opaque field
cad.placement: Over prepared and sealed ceiling
cad.opening: Exclude lights, grilles and access panels as scheduled

notes: Flat and matt are product sheen descriptions with measured or declared ranges; do not assume identical values across brands.

objects.name: water-borne enamel paint
objects.definition: A water-borne opaque finish coating formulated to provide a harder, more cleanable enamel-type surface on prepared doors, trim and selected walls.
functions: Provide a durable opaque finish
Create a cleanable handled surface
Follow detailed trim and joinery geometry

cad.pattern: Opaque film following trim, leaf and frame faces
cad.placement: Over compatible primer or undercoat
cad.opening: Exclude seals, labels, hardware and moving contacts

notes: Enamel describes the finish class and properties here, not one mandatory solvent or sheen.

objects.name: solvent-borne alkyd enamel
objects.definition: An opaque solvent-borne finish coating based principally on an alkyd binder, used on compatible prepared trim, doors and selected metal or timber surfaces.
functions: Provide a hard opaque service finish
Flow over detailed joinery and trim
Complete a compatible alkyd coating build-up

cad.pattern: Opaque film following detailed host faces
cad.placement: Over compatible prepared primer or undercoat
cad.opening: Exclude seals, labels, hardware and contacts

notes: Oil-based is common trade language but does not precisely identify every alkyd formulation.

objects.name: exterior acrylic finish coat
objects.definition: An opaque exterior water-borne acrylic coating used as the exposed weathering finish over a compatible prepared wall, cladding, render or trim system.
functions: Provide exterior colour
Protect the surface within documented exposure limits
Form the exposed maintainable coating face

cad.pattern: Continuous exterior opaque field
cad.placement: Over compatible primed exterior substrate
cad.opening: Return and terminate around joints, flashings and openings

notes: Where the coating is relied on for external-wall weatherproofing, retain the product evidence and full wall-system relationship required by NCC Part A5.

objects.name: smooth masonry finish coat
objects.definition: An opaque coating that leaves a substantially smooth painted face on prepared concrete, cement render or masonry without an intentionally aggregate-filled relief profile.
functions: Provide smooth opaque colour
Form the exposed mineral-surface finish
Keep smooth paint distinct from texture coating and render

cad.pattern: Smooth continuous mineral-surface field
cad.placement: Over compatible masonry primer or sealer
cad.opening: Stop at joints and excluded interfaces

notes: A smooth finish coat follows rather than corrects the actual substrate geometry.

objects.name: low-profile texture coating
objects.definition: A decorative coating containing fine aggregate or rheology that intentionally leaves a shallow relief pattern on prepared concrete, render or masonry.
functions: Create a fine textured face
Reduce visual prominence of minor surface variation
Provide a maintainable coloured coating

cad.pattern: Fine procedural relief mapped to the true coated surface
cad.placement: Over prepared and sealed mineral substrate
cad.opening: Stop at movement joints, flashings and trim

notes: Texture depth and tool pattern are geometry or appearance attributes; the coating remains a separate physical layer from render.

objects.name: aggregate-filled high-build texture coating
objects.definition: A latex-bound coating with mineral aggregate applied at a visibly raised build to produce a pronounced texture on prepared concrete, render or masonry.
functions: Create a pronounced relief texture
Provide substantial coating build
Carry the nominated colour or receive a compatible protective topcoat

cad.pattern: Raised procedural relief with documented aggregate and tool pattern
cad.placement: Over compatible sealed concrete, render or masonry
cad.opening: Respect movement joints and flashings

notes: High-build is relative to ordinary paint; record actual declared build or profile instead of assigning a universal thickness.

objects.name: texture-coating protective topcoat
objects.definition: A separate compatible coat applied over an aggregate-filled texture layer where the documented system uses it to complete colour, cleanability or weathering performance.
functions: Seal the exposed texture surface
Provide uniform colour or sheen
Improve maintainability within the documented system

cad.pattern: Thin conformal coat following raised texture
cad.placement: Over the dry compatible texture layer
cad.opening: Stop at joints and excluded surfaces

notes: Not every self-coloured texture needs a separate topcoat; create this object only when the system includes one.

objects.name: clear masonry sealer
objects.definition: A transparent or near-transparent coating applied to prepared concrete, masonry or render to modify surface absorption or service behaviour while leaving the substrate visible.
functions: Retain visible mineral appearance
Reduce absorption within documented capability
Provide a maintainable clear surface treatment
materials: penetrating silane or siloxane treatment where selected

cad.pattern: Transparent bounded treatment field
cad.placement: On compatible prepared mineral surface
cad.opening: Respect joints and adjacent finish changes
cad.load: Thin film or shallow penetrating treatment

notes: Clear does not mean invisible, waterproof or vapour-open; those are separate product properties requiring evidence.

objects.name: wet-area decorative paint
objects.definition: An exposed decorative coating selected for a humid or intermittently splashed internal location, installed over the required lining and waterproofing construction rather than replacing it.
functions: Provide colour and a cleanable exposed face
Tolerate the documented room exposure
Keep the decorative layer separate from the waterproofing system

cad.pattern: Bounded decorative field outside or over compliant wet-area construction as selected
cad.placement: On compatible prepared wet-area lining or ceiling
cad.opening: Coordinate fixtures, sealants and tiled areas

notes: Never use this object to satisfy waterproofing geometry; it is decorative paint even when marketed for bathrooms.

objects.name: decorative effect base coat
objects.definition: The uniform first visible colour layer beneath a glaze, metallic, pearlescent, mottled or other worked decorative effect.
functions: Set the background colour
Provide a compatible working surface
Remain visible through or between later effect material

cad.pattern: Uniform colour field beneath procedural effect
cad.placement: Over prepared primer or undercoat
cad.opening: Follow the approved decorative field

notes: The base coat is physically distinct even when the final rendered texture visually blends it with the effect layer.

objects.name: decorative glaze coat
objects.definition: A transparent or translucent coloured coating worked over a compatible base coat to produce layered, mottled, dragged, washed or similar decorative variation.
functions: Create translucent colour variation
Reveal the base coat through the effect
Carry the recorded tool direction and working pattern

cad.pattern: Procedural translucent pattern over the base field
cad.placement: On dry compatible decorative base coat
cad.opening: Keep pattern continuity around openings as documented

notes: Application tool, direction and scale should be model parameters; a flat colour swatch cannot describe the physical finish.

objects.name: metallic effect coat
objects.definition: A decorative coating containing metallic or metal-effect flakes that produces direction-sensitive sparkle or lustre over a compatible prepared base.
functions: Create metallic visual response
Retain application direction and overlap effects
Form the selected exposed or clear-protected decorative layer

cad.pattern: Direction-sensitive procedural metallic field
cad.placement: Over the documented compatible base coat
cad.opening: Preserve stroke or spray direction through returns

notes: Metallic appearance depends on light and flake orientation; do not model this as a solid metal plate.

objects.name: pearlescent effect coat
objects.definition: A decorative coating containing interference or pearlescent pigments that changes lustre or apparent colour with viewing and lighting conditions.
functions: Create a pearlescent visual response
Layer translucent effect over a base colour
Retain direction and sample-approved appearance

cad.pattern: View-dependent procedural effect field
cad.placement: Over compatible base colour
cad.opening: Keep direction consistent through documented returns

notes: A physically based render material may show the effect, but the product and coat remain the quantity-bearing object.

objects.name: magnetic-receptive paint
objects.definition: A heavy decorative base coating containing ferrous material so magnets can be attracted to the finished wall when the documented system and build are provided.
functions: Provide a magnet-attracting wall field
Create build beneath the decorative topcoat
Keep functional field boundaries explicit

cad.pattern: Bounded functional coating field beneath decorative topcoat
cad.placement: On compatible prepared internal wall
cad.opening: Coordinate switches, outlets and trim

notes: The dry film is not itself a permanent magnet; performance depends on product build, topcoats and the magnets used.

objects.name: chalkboard paint
objects.definition: A hard, low-glare finish coating intended to form a reusable chalk-writing field on a suitably smooth prepared surface.
functions: Provide a chalk-writing surface
Define a cleanable functional wall or panel field
Carry colour and field-edge geometry

cad.pattern: Bounded smooth writing field
cad.placement: On compatible smooth prepared wall, door or panel
cad.opening: Coordinate border, trim and fittings

notes: Chalkboard performance comes from the selected coating system, not merely a black colour and matt sheen.

objects.name: water-borne clear timber coating
objects.definition: A transparent or near-transparent water-borne film finish applied to prepared timber so the grain remains visible while the surface gains the documented protection and sheen.
functions: Leave timber grain visible
Form a protective clear film
Provide the selected sheen and maintainable face

cad.pattern: Transparent film following timber faces and edges
cad.placement: Over prepared timber or compatible stain
cad.opening: Exclude hardware, seals and uncoated joints

notes: Use the existing floor-specific coating object for timber floors; this object covers other architectural timber unless product evidence says otherwise.

objects.name: solvent-borne timber varnish
objects.definition: A transparent or translucent solvent-borne film finish that dries or cures over prepared timber to leave the grain visible beneath a protective surface.
functions: Form a clear protective film
Enhance or warm visible timber colour
Provide the selected sheen and service resistance
materials: alkyd, oil-modified or other varnish resin

cad.pattern: Transparent conformal timber film
cad.placement: Over prepared timber or compatible sealed and stained face
cad.opening: Follow joinery faces and exclude hardware

notes: Varnish is a family of film-forming finishes, not a synonym for every clear liquid timber product.

objects.name: polyurethane clear timber coating
objects.definition: A clear film-forming timber coating whose cured binder is polyurethane or polyurethane-modified, selected for the relevant internal or external architectural surface.
functions: Form a tough transparent film
Protect visible timber
Provide the scheduled sheen and service properties
materials: one- or two-component polyurethane where selected

cad.pattern: Transparent multi-coat film following timber geometry
cad.placement: Over prepared timber or compatible stain and sealer
cad.opening: Exclude hardware, seals and uncoated contacts

notes: Polyurethane identifies binder chemistry; water-borne versus solvent-borne and one- versus two-component remain required attributes.

objects.name: clear lacquer coating
objects.definition: A fast-drying clear film finish, commonly spray-applied to compatible internal timber, joinery or furniture-like building components as part of a documented lacquer system.
functions: Form a smooth transparent film
Provide a fast-built internal finish
Retain visible timber grain
materials: nitrocellulose, acrylic or other lacquer resin

cad.pattern: Thin transparent spray or brushed film
cad.placement: On compatible prepared internal timber
cad.opening: Exclude fittings and joints

notes: Lacquer describes a finish family, not a universal durability class or permission for external use.

objects.name: shellac sealer coat
objects.definition: A thin shellac-based coat used as a clear or amber sealer, barrier or traditional finish on compatible prepared timber within a documented coating build-up.
functions: Seal timber
Provide a barrier between compatible layers
Contribute a clear or warm-toned traditional film
attributes: role as sealer or exposed finish

cad.pattern: Thin transparent or amber conformal film
cad.placement: On compatible prepared timber or between compatible finish layers
cad.opening: Follow timber component geometry

notes: French polishing is a multi-pass technique and finish system; one shellac coat is not automatically a complete French-polished assembly.

objects.name: hardwax-oil timber finish
objects.definition: A timber finish based on drying oils and waxes that penetrates and leaves a thin surface-enriched finish rather than a conventional thick clear varnish film.
functions: Enhance visible timber
Provide a low-build protective surface
Permit product-specific local maintenance or renewal
materials: solvent or water carrier during application

cad.pattern: Shallow penetrating field with very low surface build
cad.placement: Within and on prepared timber
cad.opening: Follow exposed timber faces

notes: Hardwax oil and floor protective coatings may share chemistry, but use the floor-specific object for finished floors.

objects.name: penetrating timber oil
objects.definition: A low-build oil finish absorbed into prepared timber, usually leaving the grain and surface texture visible with limited film above the face.
functions: Enhance timber colour and grain
Reduce absorption within documented capability
Provide a renewable exposed finish

cad.pattern: Penetrating finish field following timber grain and faces
cad.placement: Within prepared timber surface
cad.opening: Treat ends and joints as documented
cad.load: Shallow absorbed finish with little surface film

notes: Oil, stain and preservative can be combined in some products, but the tool must store the declared physical and performance roles rather than infer them from colour.

objects.name: water-borne timber stain
objects.definition: A water-borne translucent or penetrating colouring treatment applied to prepared timber to change its apparent colour while leaving grain visible.
functions: Colour timber
Retain visible grain
Provide the colour layer beneath a compatible clear finish or as a declared exterior stain system

cad.pattern: Translucent colour field retaining grain map
cad.placement: On and within prepared timber beneath compatible finish where required
cad.opening: Follow timber faces and end treatment

notes: The same named stain can look different on different species, cuts and preparation; store the physical timber and approved sample.

objects.name: solvent-borne timber stain
objects.definition: A solvent-borne translucent or penetrating colouring treatment used to change prepared timber colour while retaining visible grain.
functions: Colour prepared timber
Retain grain visibility
Provide a compatible colour layer beneath the selected finish

cad.pattern: Translucent colour field retaining timber grain
cad.placement: Within prepared timber surface
cad.opening: Follow timber faces and end treatment

notes: Solvent-borne does not automatically mean oil finish; stain colour and later clear-film chemistry remain separate facts.

objects.name: exterior semi-transparent timber stain
objects.definition: A pigmented exterior timber coating that leaves grain partly visible while providing documented colour and weathering protection with lower opacity than paint.
functions: Colour exterior timber while retaining grain
Reduce UV exposure within documented capability
Provide a maintainable exterior stain finish
materials: water or solvent carrier during application

cad.pattern: Translucent weather-exposed timber field
cad.placement: On prepared exterior timber
cad.opening: Treat faces, edges, ends and joints as documented

notes: Semi-transparent is an opacity description, not a universal film thickness or maintenance interval.

objects.name: clear topcoat over timber stain
objects.definition: A compatible transparent protective film applied over a dried timber stain where the complete selected system requires a separate clear topcoat.
functions: Protect the stained surface
Provide the final sheen and service face
Keep the colouring layer separate from the protective film
materials: polyurethane or other compatible clear finish

cad.pattern: Transparent film following the stained timber field
cad.placement: Over compatible dry timber stain
cad.opening: Follow timber faces and exclusions

notes: Some products combine stain and film finish; create this separate object only when a separate clear layer is physically installed.

objects.name: wallpaper supply roll
objects.definition: A factory-wound supply unit of wallpaper or roll-format wallcovering from which installed drops, panels, borders or lining lengths are cut.
functions: Supply measurable covering area
Carry batch, width, length and pattern-repeat data
Support cutting and waste calculations

cad.pattern: Cylindrical supply representation linked to cut-layout data
cad.placement: Off-model supply or quantity schedule, not on the finished wall
cad.opening: Not applicable to installed opening geometry

notes: The roll is useful for estimating but is not part of the completed wall; installed geometry is represented by drops or panels.

objects.name: installed wallpaper drop
objects.definition: One cut length of roll-format wallpaper hung as a sheet from the set-out line, usually vertically, and trimmed at its top, bottom, openings and junctions.
functions: Cover one strip of prepared wall
Carry a portion of the pattern
Create measurable side seams with adjacent drops

cad.pattern: Repeated cut sheets with pattern-alignment offset
cad.placement: On the prepared wall from a plumb set-out datum
cad.opening: Trim and continue around openings as documented
cad.load: Light flexible sheet bonded across its back

notes: Draw actual finished drop edges and pattern offsets; do not infer seam-free continuity from a tiled texture image.

objects.name: paper wallpaper
objects.definition: A decorative wallcovering whose principal face and backing are paper-based, installed in drops with a compatible wall preparation and adhesive method.
functions: Provide a printed or coloured decorative face
Form cuttable drops
Receive or work with the selected wallpaper adhesive

cad.pattern: Repeated flexible paper drops with printed pattern
cad.placement: On prepared primed or sized wall
cad.opening: Trim around fittings and openings
cad.load: Light paper sheet bonded to wall

notes: Paper construction can expand or relax when pasted; keep the product's hanging method rather than assigning one universal booking time.

objects.name: non-woven wallpaper
objects.definition: A wallpaper made with a dimensionally stable non-woven fibre backing or body, commonly installed by applying compatible paste to the wall where the product directs.
functions: Provide a decorative sheet face
Limit wet expansion relative to conventional paper products
Support paste-the-wall or other documented installation

cad.pattern: Repeated dimensionally stable drops
cad.placement: On prepared wall using documented adhesive topology
cad.opening: Trim around openings and fittings
cad.load: Light non-woven sheet bonded to wall

notes: Non-woven describes construction, not a guarantee that every product uses paste-the-wall installation or dry-strips cleanly.

objects.name: woven textile wallcovering
objects.definition: A decorative wallcovering with a woven textile face, usually bonded to a backing and installed in directional drops with product-specific adhesive and seam handling.
functions: Provide a woven decorative face
Carry fibre direction and weave texture
Form repeated specialist drops or panels

cad.pattern: Directional woven drops with visible textile texture
cad.placement: On smooth prepared wall with compatible specialist adhesive
cad.opening: Trim with product-specific edge control
cad.load: Flexible textile-faced sheet bonded to wall

notes: Fire, acoustic or impact performance must be attached only when tested for the complete selected wallcovering system.

objects.name: vinyl-coated paper wallpaper
objects.definition: A paper-backed wallpaper carrying a thin vinyl or polymer face coating that improves the declared surface cleanability while retaining paper as the main backing.
functions: Provide printed decoration
Provide a coated cleanable face
Form roll-cut wallpaper drops
materials: thin vinyl or polymer face coating

cad.pattern: Printed coated-paper drops
cad.placement: On prepared wall with compatible adhesive
cad.opening: Trim at openings and fittings

notes: Vinyl-coated paper is not the same construction as a thicker solid-vinyl face, so keep backing and face data explicit.

objects.name: solid-vinyl wallcovering
objects.definition: A wallcovering with a substantial continuous vinyl face layer carried on a paper, fabric or non-woven backing and installed with a compatible heavy-duty adhesive.
functions: Provide a durable decorative vinyl face
Resist cleaning and abrasion within declared limits
Form cut specialist drops

cad.pattern: Flexible vinyl-faced drops with exact seam geometry
cad.placement: On prepared wall using product-compatible adhesive
cad.opening: Trim and seal only as the selected product requires
cad.load: Flexible vinyl-faced sheet bonded to wall

notes: Do not substitute this decorative object for a classified wet-area vinyl wall-sheet system.

objects.name: linen-backed vinyl wallcovering
objects.definition: A durable vinyl-faced wallcovering laminated to a woven linen or fabric backing, installed in heavy specialist drops with compatible adhesive and seam preparation.
functions: Provide a robust decorative vinyl face
Use fabric backing for dimensional and handling behaviour
Form durable specialist wallcovering drops

cad.pattern: Heavy fabric-backed drops with directional face
cad.placement: On smooth prepared wall with specialist adhesive
cad.opening: Trim using product-specific detail

notes: Linen-backed describes the backing construction; it does not mean the visible face is linen.

objects.name: grasscloth wallcovering
objects.definition: A handmade or machine-arranged natural-fibre wallcovering in which grasses, reeds or similar fibres form the visible face on a backing sheet.
functions: Provide a natural linear fibre texture
Form directional decorative drops
Retain intended panel-to-panel variation
materials: grass, reed, jute or similar natural fibre
not_synonyms: paper printed to look like grasscloth

cad.pattern: Directional natural-fibre drops with deliberately visible variation
cad.placement: On smooth prepared wall with product-specific adhesive
cad.opening: Trim without contaminating the sensitive face

notes: Panel shading, fibre irregularity and visible seams may be inherent; the tool should not mark all variation as installation error.

objects.name: flock wallcovering
objects.definition: A decorative wallcovering with short fibres electrostatically or adhesively deposited in a raised pattern on a paper, non-woven or textile base.
functions: Provide a raised velvet-like pattern
Create directional light response
Form specialist drops with sensitive face handling

cad.pattern: Repeated raised flock pattern with pile direction
cad.placement: On prepared wall using compatible adhesive
cad.opening: Trim while protecting raised face

notes: Pile direction changes appearance with light; preserve a common top direction unless the design intentionally varies it.

objects.name: metallic-foil wallcovering
objects.definition: A wallcovering with a thin metallic foil or metallised decorative face laminated to a flexible backing and installed on an exceptionally smooth compatible substrate.
functions: Provide a reflective metallic face
Form flexible decorative drops
Reveal or control substrate and seam geometry through a smooth finish
materials: thin metal foil or metallised film

cad.pattern: Reflective directional flexible drops
cad.placement: On very smooth prepared wall with compatible adhesive
cad.opening: Trim without creasing reflective face

notes: A decorative foil face does not automatically provide electrical shielding, fire performance or a solid metal lining.

objects.name: embossed paintable wallpaper
objects.definition: A relief-pattern paper wallcovering intended to be installed in drops and commonly painted after hanging, including products often described by the legacy proprietary term anaglypta.
functions: Provide a repeating raised paper relief
Cover a prepared wall with paintable texture
Carry a later compatible decorative paint film

cad.pattern: Repeated embossed relief sheets with later conformal paint
cad.placement: On prepared wall with compatible adhesive
cad.opening: Align relief and trim at openings

notes: Anaglypta began as a proprietary name and is not a reliable synonym for every raised wallcovering construction.

objects.name: moulded relief wallcovering
objects.definition: A relatively heavy wallcovering with a moulded or deeply embossed relief face, commonly supplied in rolls and often painted or otherwise finished after installation.
functions: Create deep decorative relief
Form repeated roll-cut wall sheets
Receive a documented paint or finish coat where required
materials: paper or fabric reinforcement where supplied

cad.pattern: Deep repeated relief sheets following wall planes
cad.placement: On strong smooth prepared substrate with product-specific adhesive
cad.opening: Coordinate relief cuts and moulded trims
cad.load: Relatively heavy relief sheet bonded to wall

notes: Use a generic canonical name and retain proprietary names as aliases; construction and mass vary between products.

objects.name: wall mural panel
objects.definition: One numbered or ordered sheet of a larger printed mural image, sized and positioned so its image edge aligns with the adjacent panel or documented overlap.
functions: Carry one portion of a continuous image
Establish panel order and crop
Create measurable mural seams

cad.pattern: Ordered non-repeating image panels
cad.placement: At its numbered position within the mural boundary
cad.opening: Crop image around openings as approved
cad.load: Light printed panel bonded to wall

notes: Panel order, overlap and crop are geometry; a generic repeating texture cannot reconstruct a mural correctly.

objects.name: wallpaper lining paper
objects.definition: A plain paper or fibre sheet installed over a prepared wall before the decorative wallcovering to create a more uniform receiving face or support the selected hanging system.
functions: Provide an intermediate paper face
Reduce minor visual surface variation
Support the compatible decorative wallcovering

cad.pattern: Plain underlayer strips with joints offset from decorative seams
cad.placement: Between prepared wall and decorative covering
cad.opening: Trim around openings and fittings
cad.load: Light paper underlayer bonded to wall

notes: Lining paper is a finish-preparation sheet, not the plasterboard, fibre-cement or solid-wall substrate.

objects.name: wallpaper border strip
objects.definition: A narrow decorative wallcovering strip installed as a horizontal, vertical or shaped band over a prepared surface or compatible base covering.
functions: Create a narrow decorative band
Form a transition or feature line
Provide measurable ends, joints and corner returns

cad.pattern: Narrow repeating decorative strip along a set-out path
cad.placement: On prepared wall or compatible installed covering
cad.start: Border endpoint or selected inconspicuous joint
cad.opening: Terminate or return around openings as designed

notes: A border has physical width and joints; it is not merely a line style or texture boundary.

objects.name: cellulose wallpaper adhesive
objects.definition: A water-mixed cellulose-based paste used to bond compatible lightweight paper or other declared wallcoverings to a suitably prepared substrate.
functions: Bond compatible covering
Provide working slip for positioning
Dry to form the installed adhesive film

cad.pattern: Continuous adhesive film behind each compatible drop
cad.placement: Between prepared substrate and covering backing
cad.opening: Follow trimmed covering geometry

notes: Select from product compatibility; cellulose chemistry does not make the paste suitable for every heavy or non-porous wallcovering.

objects.name: starch wallpaper adhesive
objects.definition: A starch-based paste used to bond compatible paper wallcoverings or lining papers to a prepared substrate, often supplied as powder or ready mix before installation.
functions: Bond compatible paper covering
Provide positioning slip
Dry as a thin installed adhesive layer

cad.pattern: Continuous thin adhesive behind paper drops
cad.placement: Between prepared wall and compatible paper backing
cad.opening: Follow trimmed drop

notes: Starch identifies the adhesive family; mixing, preservatives and wallcovering compatibility remain product-specific.

objects.name: PVA wallcovering adhesive
objects.definition: A polyvinyl-acetate-based adhesive used alone or as a documented additive for compatible heavier, less absorbent or specialist wallcoverings.
functions: Provide a stronger wallcovering bond
Bond selected specialist backings
Dry as the permanent adhesive film

cad.pattern: Continuous or selected strengthened adhesive field
cad.placement: Between prepared substrate and compatible specialist backing
cad.opening: Follow sheet and seam detail

notes: Do not substitute a generic woodworking adhesive; use a product and mix documented for the wallcovering and substrate.

objects.name: latex wallcovering adhesive
objects.definition: A formulated latex or polymer-dispersion adhesive used for compatible commercial vinyl, textile, foil or other specialist wallcoverings requiring a durable bond.
functions: Bond heavy or specialist covering
Provide product-specific tack and working time
Remain as a flexible installed adhesive film

cad.pattern: Continuous specialist adhesive field
cad.placement: Between prepared wall and heavy compatible wallcovering
cad.opening: Follow trimmed covering and seam detail

notes: Latex is broad trade language; store the selected product and compatibility rather than inferring one chemistry.

objects.name: factory-applied ready-paste coating
objects.definition: A dry factory-applied adhesive coating on the back of pre-pasted wallpaper that is activated by the documented wetting method before the sheet is hung.
functions: Carry adhesive with the wallpaper
Activate during installation
Form the permanent bond after hanging and drying

cad.pattern: Continuous factory coating on the back of each sheet
cad.placement: Between wallpaper backing and prepared wall after activation
cad.opening: Follow trimmed wallpaper geometry

notes: Pre-pasted means water-activated factory adhesive; it is not the same as peel-and-stick pressure-sensitive material.

objects.name: pressure-sensitive wallcovering adhesive backing
objects.definition: A tacky factory-applied adhesive layer on a self-adhesive wallcovering that bonds under placement pressure after its temporary release liner is removed.
functions: Bond the self-adhesive sheet without wet paste
Remain attached to the installed covering
Carry declared repositionability or removability properties

cad.pattern: Continuous factory adhesive backing behind each panel
cad.placement: Between self-adhesive face sheet and compatible prepared wall
cad.opening: Follow trimmed panel geometry

notes: The release liner is temporary packaging and is deliberately excluded from the completed-building object.

objects.name: wallcovering butt seam
objects.definition: The finished narrow junction where two trimmed wallcovering edges meet edge-to-edge without an intentional face overlap.
functions: Join adjacent drops visually
Define measurable sheet boundaries
Carry pattern-match and edge-condition information

cad.pattern: Zero- or near-zero-width meeting line between adjacent sheets
cad.placement: At the common finished edge of two drops
cad.opening: Continue or terminate at opening cuts

notes: A seam is real installed geometry even if rendered nearly invisible; keep it for quantities, repairs and pattern alignment.

objects.name: double-cut wallcovering seam
objects.definition: A finished butt seam produced by overlapping adjacent wallcovering edges during installation and cutting through both layers so the retained edges meet on the same cut line.
functions: Create matching cut edges on heavy or non-pretrimmed material
Form a close finished butt joint
Record the seam method and protected substrate condition

cad.pattern: Single finished joint line derived from paired overlapped cuts
cad.placement: At adjacent specialist wallcovering edges
cad.opening: Coordinate intersections and openings
cad.load: Finished butt junction, not a retained double thickness

notes: The temporary overlap and trimmed waste are installation states; the completed object is the close butt seam.

objects.name: wallcovering internal-corner return
objects.definition: The narrow portion of a wallcovering drop carried through an internal corner onto the adjoining wall before the next sheet is set out or overlapped as documented.
functions: Maintain covering continuity into the corner
Avoid relying on a full-width out-of-plumb wrap
Provide a controlled base for the next wall's first drop

cad.pattern: Narrow flexible strip folded through concave corner
cad.placement: From one wall face around the internal corner onto the next
cad.opening: Interrupt at intersecting trim or openings

notes: Return width is geometry chosen from wall plumb and product behaviour, not one universal dimension.

objects.name: wallcovering external-corner wrap
objects.definition: The portion of a compatible wallcovering sheet wrapped around a convex external corner onto the adjoining face where the product and corner condition permit it.
functions: Keep the decorative face continuous around a corner
Move the sheet edge away from the corner arris
Carry pattern and direction through the return

cad.pattern: Flexible sheet folded around convex corner
cad.placement: Across the external corner arris onto the adjacent wall
cad.opening: Stop or transition at trim and intersections

notes: Stiff, brittle or deeply textured coverings may need a cut, trim or specialist detail instead of a wrap.

objects.name: wallcovering trimmed edge
objects.definition: The finished cut edge where a wallcovering terminates against a ceiling, skirting, opening, fitting, trim, feature boundary or other documented stop.
functions: Define the installed covering boundary
Create a clean junction with adjacent construction
Record cut path and exposed-edge condition
attributes: seal or trim if separately specified

cad.pattern: Continuous boundary line following adjacent construction
cad.placement: At the perimeter of each installed wallcovering field
cad.opening: Trace openings, fittings and finish changes

notes: The edge is not assumed sealed; add a separate trim or seal only when physically specified.

objects.name: wallcovering seam-edge colour coating
objects.definition: A very narrow compatible colour treatment applied to selected wallcovering cut edges so a contrasting backing is less visible at the finished seam or termination.
functions: Reduce visible light-coloured cut edges
Coordinate dark or strongly coloured face material
Keep the edge treatment distinct from face paint
materials: compatible artist pastel or product-approved edge colour

cad.pattern: Very narrow linear coating on the cut sheet edge
cad.placement: On selected wallcovering edge before final seam closure
cad.opening: Follow seam or termination cut

notes: Create this object only when an actual compatible edge-colouring treatment is specified; do not fake seam closure by widening the face texture.
